title: Safety corridor for GPU memory slicing and KV pressure management
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see transient OOMs and elevated tail latency on mixed workloads when continuous batching and aggressive KV caching combine with model weight residency pressure. Existing memory budgeting heuristics allocate static fractions for weights, KV cache, and activations which fail to adapt quickly to sudden prefix-heavy workloads or tenant burst patterns. This ticket defines, implements, and validates a dynamic 'safety corridor' approach that maintains a moving memory reserve and a set of eviction/gating policies to avoid OOMs while preserving throughput and cache utility.

Goals: 1) Reduce OOM incidents attributable to KV growth or activation surges by >= 90% in canary clusters. 2) Keep P99 latency regression < 10% relative to baseline. 3) Limit additional per-token cost (due to reduced batching or extra evictions) to < 7%. 4) Produce observability surfaces (telemetry and dashboards) that expose the corridor state and decisions in real time.

Proposed design (high-level):
- Memory safety corridor: maintain three logical buckets on each GPU: weights (W), kv_cache (K), activations/reserved_headroom (A). Instead of fixed percentiles, compute a dynamic safety corridor S(t) = base_reserve + alpha * recent_kv_derivative + beta * activation_peak_signal. S(t) is the buffer subtracted from available free memory before admitting larger continuous-batched requests.
- Corridor inputs: telemetry stream includes kv_growth_rate (tokens/sec added to KV), kv_hit_ratio, activation_peak_ratio (observed activation bytes / baseline for request shape), queued_batch_size_distribution, and GPU_free_fraction.
- Admission control: before inflating a batch into the runtime, simulate expected delta for weights (static per model), kv_delta (predicted by prefix length and kv_policy), and activation_delta (estimated by request shape and batch multiplier). If sum(delta) + current_usage + S(t) > physical_mem_limit, then apply the lowest-cost mitigation from the policy stack: 1) reduce batch size (continuous batching fallback step), 2) selectively evict older KV segments (least-recently-used by tenant-scoped epoch), 3) fall back to a smaller quantized model variant (if pinned policy allows), 4) reject request with clear error code and retry instructions.
- Eviction policy: tenant-aware, age-weighted LRU with soft TTL for prompt-based KV segments. Evictions record impact on downstream latency and quality; we will capture quality regressions with a lightweight eval pipeline that replays evicted prefixes against small probe prompts.
- Learning component: a short-window linear predictor (or light exponential smoothing) estimates kv_growth_rate and activation_peak_signal; parameters will be tunable per cluster profile. Longer-term, we will evaluate a probabilistic learner (future ticket) to tune alpha/beta per workload mix.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Instrumentation shims (1 sprint): add per-tenant KV growth telemetry, batch shape histograms, and an API to query simulated memory deltas for a proposed batch.
2) Safety corridor library (1 sprint): implement S(t) computation, config flags, and local policy engine for admission/veto decisions. Expose metrics: corridor_value, corridor_trigger_count, admission_rejections, eviction_count, eviction_bytes, predicted_kv_delta.
3) Canary rollout (2 sprints): wire into canary runtime clusters with conservative defaults (base_reserve=6% of GPU RAM, alpha=0.6, beta=0.4). Run with a circuit-breaker that auto-rolls back to static allocation if P99 latency or throughput cost thresholds are breached.
4) Observability and dashboards (parallel): add Grafana panels and alert rules; surface corridor state per-GPU, per-tenant, and per-model.
5) Evaluation & tuning (1 sprint): run A/B against baseline workloads (prefix-heavy chat, short-turn QA, embedding-heavy inference) and adjust alpha/beta and mitigation ordering.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary runs for 72 hours with no repeatable OOM pattern and OOM rate reduced by >= 90%.
- P99 latency degradation <= 10% and throughput loss <= 8% for target workloads.
- Dashboards show corridor triggers and decision reasons per incident and link to the eviction traces.
- PRs merged with unit tests for corridor computation and integration tests for admission decisions.

Rollout and safety: Start with 5% of traffic on non-critical canaries, slowly increase to 25% and 60% once canary success criteria pass. Keep an automated rollback gate tied to incident response and PagerDuty. Document the new error codes and recommended client retry behavior in the API docs.

Instrumentation & dashboards:
- New metrics: runtime.corridor.value, runtime.corridor.trigger, runtime.admission.rejects, runtime.eviction.count, runtime.eviction.kv_bytes, runtime.kv.growth_rate, runtime.batch.shape_p50/p95/p99.
- Dashboards: corridor overview, per-tenant corridor history, eviction impact timeline, admission decision trace links.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-aggressive corridor reduces batching and increases cost. Mitigation: conservative defaults, gradual ramp, and cost telemetry to revert.
- Risk: Evictions create quality regressions for chat continuity. Mitigation: tenant-scoped soft TTLs and replay probe evaluations to detect regressions quickly.
- Risk: Metrics lag causes incorrect S(t). Mitigation: use short windows (1s–5s) and fall back to static reserve on telemetry outage.

Open questions:
- Should corridor be global per-GPU or per-tenant per-GPU slice? (Initial implementation: per-GPU with tenant annotations; follow-up will evaluate per-tenant slicing for high-commit tenants.)
- Optimal alpha/beta ranges for each cluster profile — need to gather telemetry in instrumentation phase.

2025-02-25 - Mike Thompson: Reviewed eviction policy. Requested we add per-tenant eviction telemetry and ensure eviction decisions include tenant_id and segment_age in traces. Marked as blocker for canary rollout until available.

2025-03-03 - Design Review (Clara Nguyen): UX for error messaging reviewed. Recommend adding explicit retry-after hints for clients when admission rejects occur due to corridor pressure.
